body:
The material exposes five facts and no interpretations: three people share a flat; they argue about chores; they sometimes agree who will do something and later disagree about what that agreement meant; their work schedules change; one friend has begun avoiding the conversations. Everything else — who does more, whether the agreements were spoken or written, why the friend avoids — is not stated, so what follows is a set of conjectures for the asker to check against what they actually know.

The most useful conjecture is that this is not primarily a fairness fight but an ambiguity problem wearing a fairness fight's clothes. An agreement that fixes who but leaves when, to what standard, and under what conditions is only half an agreement; the missing halves get filled in later by each party, sincerely and differently. That would explain the otherwise odd feature of the disputes — that they are about meaning rather than about refusal. Nobody has to be lying for this to recur; the shared record simply never existed.

The second conjecture concerns the schedules. An agreement made under one roster can become unmeetable under another, and where there is no cheap, explicit way to renegotiate, the natural move is silence — which the others will read as defiance. Some of what looks like bad faith may be changed feasibility with no exit route. This also makes the avoidance partly intelligible: if the conversations have become aversive recycling of unwinnable 'what did we mean' disputes, avoiding them is locally rational. But the avoidance could equally be about something else — the friendship, feeling policed, life outside the flat — and the material cannot tell these apart. Both readings, though, point to the same first move: change the format of coordination so it costs less, and ask rather than diagnose.

What the asker can actually do, with two co-decision-makers and one of them withdrawing, is propose, not enforce.

First, stop litigating the past. What an ambiguous agreement meant cannot be reconstructed, only superseded. Say once, at a calm moment, that old disputed agreements are off the table and future ones start fresh — then hold to it, even when relitigating would feel satisfying.

Second, make the next agreements checkable. One shared place — a whiteboard, a shared note, an app — where every agreement names the task, the owner, a deadline, and one line on what 'done' looks like. The point is shared memory, not surveillance, and offering it as a two-week trial lets the others amend or drop it rather than resist it.

Third, build the schedules in. A standing rule: if your schedule changes and you can't do what you claimed, say so by an agreed day and it gets re-dealt. This gives silence somewhere to go besides defiance, and makes the system bend with the very constraint that keeps breaking it.

Fourth, re-approach the avoidant friend at their cost level: ask which format they would actually tolerate — a ten-minute, time-boxed check-in, or messages if that is what they will answer — and offer the trial in that form, framed as making life easier for everyone rather than holding anyone to account. Asking also gathers information about why they avoid, without forcing a diagnosis on them.

Three failure modes deserve naming. A written system among friends can read as distrust, and the record can be repurposed as a charge sheet; the mitigations are the trial framing, a light tone, and an explicit norm that the board is a memory aid, not evidence. Whoever runs the system has acquired a new unrecorded chore — if that is the asker alone, the fix breeds the resentment it was meant to cure, so facilitation should rotate. And most important: if the real issue is that one person in fact does much more, or if the avoidance is about the friendship with chores merely where it surfaces, tidier coordination will not touch it, and the honest move is a different conversation, at a calm moment unrelated to any dispute. This account cannot tell which situation the asker is in; only they can check. The two-week trial doubles as a diagnostic — if a clean slate, a shared record, and a cheap exit route do not reduce the friction, that is evidence the problem was never about the form of the agreements at all.

This is a conjecture from the stated pattern, not an established fact about this flat.","scope":"the flat-share described in the task","grounds":"the task statement reports agreements that are later contested as to their meaning, with nothing further specified about their form or content"},{"id":"r2","type":"claim","text":"Changing work schedules plausibly convert good-faith agreements into unmeetable ones, and where no cheap renegotiation channel exists the natural response is silence, which the others will tend to read as defiance. Conjecture, not established.","scope":"chore performance under the flat's changing schedules","grounds":"the task statement reports that work schedules change"},{"id":"r3","type":"claim","text":"The asker's effective power is to propose rather than enforce: with two co-decision-makers, one of whom is described as avoiding the conversations, a system only works if offered as something the others can accept, amend, or drop.","grounds":"the task statement describes three co-residents and one who avoids the conversations"},{"id":"r4","type":"problem","text":"Why the one friend avoids the conversations is undetermined: the talks may have become aversive recycling of unwinnable 'what did we mean' disputes, or the avoidance may concern the friendship or life outside the flat, with chores merely where it surfaces. The exposed material cannot distinguish these readings, and a response should not assume either.","grounds":"the task statement reports avoidance without cause"},{"id":"r5","type":"commitment","text":"Stop adjudicating past ambiguous agreements and declare a clean slate for future ones: what a past loose agreement meant cannot be reconstructed, only superseded.","scope":"future chore coordination among the three flatmates","action":"the asker says once, at a calm moment, that old disputed agreements are off the table and future ones start fresh; thereafter declines to relitigate old meanings and redirects to wording the next agreement better","consequence":"the recurring memory-dispute loses its object, and argument shifts toward writing better next agreements","grounds":"the conjecture in r1 that the disputes stem from underspecification rather than refusal"},{"id":"r6","type":"commitment","text":"Move future chore agreements onto one shared, persistent medium — whiteboard, shared note, or app — where each entry names task, owner, deadline, and a one-line done-criterion, offered as a two-week trial.","scope":"the three flatmates' chore agreements","action":"set up the medium; at a calm moment propose the entry format and trial length; let the others amend both","consequence":"later disagreement becomes a matter of checking a record rather than reconstructing memory, and the trial framing keeps the proposal from being an imposition","depends":["r5"],"grounds":"r1 on underspecification and r3 on the asker's proposal-only power"},{"id":"r7","type":"commitment","text":"Build schedule-change into the system with a standing rule: a schedule change that blocks a claimed task triggers a say-so by an agreed day and a re-deal.","scope":"renegotiation under changing work schedules","action":"propose the rule alongside the shared medium and agree the say-so day jointly","consequence":"silence under a changed schedule stops being interpretable as defiance, and the system bends with the constraint that keeps breaking it","depends":["r6"],"grounds":"r2 on feasibility events being misread as bad faith"},{"id":"r8","type":"commitment","text":"Re-approach the avoidant friend at a cost level they may accept: ask which format they would actually tolerate — a ten-minute time-boxed check-in or asynchronous messages — and offer the trial in that form, framed as convenience rather than accountability. Ask; do not diagnose.","scope":"re-engaging the friend who avoids the conversations","action":"a low-stakes approach, in the friend's preferred channel if known, asking about format and offering the two-week trial in that form","consequence":"re-engagement is offered at a cost the avoidance may be tracking, and the asking gathers information without forcing a diagnosis on the friend","depends":["r6"],"grounds":"r4, that the cause of the avoidance is unknown, and r3, that the asker can only propose"},{"id":"r9","type":"objection","text":"A written chore system among friends can be experienced as bureaucracy or distrust, and the record can be repurposed as a charge sheet in arguments, possibly deepening the avoidance it was meant to ease.","bearing":"cuts against r6 and r7 as stated; mitigations are the trial framing, a deliberately light tone, an explicit norm that the record is a memory aid and not evidence, and willingness to drop the system if the trial makes things worse","target":["r6","r7"]},{"id":"r10","type":"objection","text":"Whoever administers the system acquires a new, unrecorded chore; if the asker alone designs and maintains it, the fix can breed the resentment it was meant to remove.","bearing":"cuts against r6 unless facilitation of the check-in and upkeep of the medium rotate, or the admin tasks are themselves listed as chores","target":["r6"]},{"id":"r11","type":"problem","text":"Whether the underlying issue is distributive — one person in fact doing much more — or the avoidance is about the friendship rather than the chores cannot be determined from the exposed material. If either holds, better coordination will not touch it, and the honest next move is a different conversation, at a calm moment unrelated to any dispute, about proportion of load or about the friendship itself.","grounds":"the task statement reports friction without any data on who does how much or on the state of the friendships","mentions":["r4"]},{"id":"r12","type":"problem","text":"Under unstable schedules the allocation principle itself — equal task counts, weighting by time at home, or by capacity — is unsettled; the trial should treat the principle as revisable at each check-in rather than settled at the outset.","mentions":["r6","r7"]}],"uptake":["r5","r6","r7","r8","r9","r10","r12"]}
